data.title: Middle East Eye: US energy chief says 'things have changed' with Hormuz, but 'not visibly'
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US energy chief says 'things have changed' with Hormuz, but 'not visibly'
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Thursday that energy supplies are flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, though “not visibly” so.
In an interview with Fox News, Wright responded to a question that gas prices have dropped even though “not much has changed with Iran” since the November 3 midterm election, saying “things actually have changed; they’re just not visibly changed.”
“We have been getting… much more oil out of the Strait of Hormuz,” Wright said, adding that “for several weeks now we’ve been getting out more refined products,” including "gasoline", "diesel" and "jet fuel".
“So the supply has indeed been growing,” he said.
This comes amid ongoing reports of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz leading to oil prices inched higher on Thursday.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund skyscraper
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund skyscraper
The skyscraper housing Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) in Riyadh was damaged on Thursday by a Houthi strike, the kingdom has confirmed.
The strike destroyed windows across seven to eight floors of the tower, Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, and bent part of its metal facade, according to a Reuters journalist. Video footage shared from the Saudi capital showed crews already working to replace the glass.
The attack is the second time this month that the Houthis have struck at the heart of Saudi Arabia’s image as a safe investment destination. PIF says it has around $1 trillion in assets. Earlier this month, the Houthis struck Aramco Tower in Riyadh.
“One of the towers of the Financial Center in Riyadh was targeted in a terrorist attack by the terrorist Houthi militia, causing material damage but no injuries -praise be to God,” the Saudi authorities said in a statement released on Thursday.
The press release included an image showing notable but relatively minor damage to the PIF headquarters. Video footage appeared to show a missile slamming into the 80-storey tower, but Middle East Eye could not independently verify the footage.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Gaza ministry demands release of detained hospital director and 81 health workers
data.author: Mee User
data.summary:
Gaza ministry demands release of detained hospital director and 81 health workers
Gaza’s health ministry has criticised Israel’s decision to extend the detention of Dr Hussam Abu Safia, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, by another six months without charge or trial, describing it as a “compound crime”.
In a statement, the ministry said Abu Safia’s continued detention violated international law, including the Geneva Conventions, which provide protections for medical and humanitarian workers.
It said 81 Palestinian health workers remained in Israeli detention, where they faced physical and psychological torture, denial of legal representation and medical neglect.
An Israeli court in Beersheba extended Abu Safia’s detention on Wednesday, rejecting his lawyer’s request for his release.
He was detained during an Israeli raid on Kamal Adwan Hospital in December 2024.
The UN human rights office has said it received information that he was subjected to torture, prolonged solitary confinement and denial of medical care.

The presidential victory of Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, or Lula, disrupted the rise of Latin America’s far right, for which subordination to US interests and diplomatic rapprochement with Israel is the order of the day.
It was a significant win. However the Brazilian far right has not disappeared.
Despite Flavio Bolsonaro’s defeat and the criminal conviction of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, the Bolsonarist Liberal Party became the largest in both houses of Congress. This reflects the enduring influence of Bolsonarismo, a right-wing ideology that promotes militarism, religious nationalism and Christian Zionism.
“I categorise Christian Zionism under the umbrella of religious nationalism,” said Ronilso Pacheco, a Brazilian theologian. “I do not view it as a separate, detached offshoot, but rather as an additional, interconnected front.”
In fact, “our evangelical fundamentalism is deeply Judaising and is committed to the unconditional defence of Israel. If this movement advances, Christian Zionism advances right along with it,” he told Middle East Eye.
This symbiosis is rooted in the manufactured theological connection between Israel and evangelicalism, particularly Pentecostalism.
